priorStories.headline: WMO reports record sea levels in 2026
priorStories.body:
Global average surface temperature from January through September was about 1.47°C above the pre-industrial average, according to the World Meteorological Organization's provisional 2026 climate assessment, released Monday.

The agency reported record sea levels and said 2026 was on track to rank among the four warmest years recorded, with a tenth consecutive year of record ocean warmth. Those full-year rankings remain provisional.

candidates.summary: Representatives of Ukraine, Russia and the United States began trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi on November 10. Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner led the US delegation; Ukraine's delegation was led by Rustem Umerov and Russia's by Vladimir Medinsky. The discussions concern security arrangements and efforts to end the war. No agreement or breakthrough was reported in the sources checked before the coverage cutoff.
candidates.title: Ukraine, Russia and US begin talks in Abu Dhabi
candidates.geography: United Arab Emirates; Ukraine; Russia; United States

candidates.summary: Ukrainian, Russian and US delegations concluded more than four hours of talks in Abu Dhabi on November 10, according to a spokesperson for Ukrainian delegation leader Rustem Umerov. President Volodymyr Zelensky said the discussions covered possible humanitarian measures, de-escalation and security guarantees for Ukraine. Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner led the US delegation, and Vladimir Medinsky led Russia's. No agreement was announced in the reporting checked.
candidates.title: Ukraine, Russia and US conclude first day of Abu Dhabi talks
candidates.geography: United Arab Emirates; Ukraine; Russia; United States

candidates.summary: The Bureau of Labor Statistics released October inflation data on November 10 at 8:30 a.m. Eastern. The Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% month over month on a seasonally adjusted basis, after September's 0.6% increase. Prices excluding food and energy rose 0.3%. Shelter increased 0.3%, food 0.5% and energy 0.7%. BLS could not publish most year-over-year comparisons because the October 2025 government shutdown prevented collection of the necessary survey data.
candidates.title: US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October

candidates.summary: Foreign Minister Anita Anand announced on November 10 that Canada was reimposing sanctions against 11 Iranian entities under its Special Economic Measures (Iran) Regulations. Global Affairs Canada attributed the measures to contributions to Iran's proliferation-sensitive nuclear activities, ballistic missile program or related financing. The entities had been delisted in 2016 following implementation of the Iran nuclear agreement. The announcement coincided with the G7 foreign ministers' meeting in Paris.
candidates.title: Canada announces renewed sanctions against 11 Iranian entities

candidates.summary: Speaking after G7 meetings in Paris on November 10, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said US sanctions and the naval blockade were exerting sufficient economic pressure on Iran that major combat operations were unnecessary. This was Rubio's assessment, not an independently established outcome. His remarks followed President Donald Trump's November 9 statement that he would hold off on additional strikes after appeals from regional governments.
candidates.title: Rubio says economic pressure on Iran removes need for major combat operations

candidates.summary: Israeli strikes and gunfire killed five people in Gaza on November 10, according to hospital authorities. Shifa Hospital reported four deaths in three strikes in Gaza City. Nasser Hospital said one person was shot dead after crossing the Yellow Line near Khan Younis. Israel's military said it struck militants in Gaza City but did not immediately comment on the Khan Younis shooting.
candidates.title: Gaza hospitals report five killed by Israeli strikes and gunfire

candidates.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth rejected the impeachment effort against him at a Pentagon news conference on November 10, arguing that the allegations concerned policy disagreements rather than impeachable offenses. Representative Thomas Massie had launched the effort on November 9 over Hegseth's handling of the Iran war and other actions. Hegseth's response was a new development; the impeachment initiative itself began the preceding day.
candidates.title: Hegseth rejects impeachment allegations at Pentagon briefing

candidates.summary: House Republicans elected Jim Jordan as their minority leader for the next Congress on November 10. He defeated Steve Scalise by 106 votes to 73, according to sources cited by ABC News. Republicans also elected Tom Emmer as minority whip and Lisa McClain as conference chair. The new leadership will serve when the next Congress begins in January.
candidates.title: House Republicans elect Jim Jordan as leader for next Congress

candidates.summary: Senate Republicans reelected John Thune as their leader on November 10, with no challenger, after discussions about their midterm losses delayed the leadership elections by several hours. John Barrasso and Tom Cotton retained their leadership positions, while Bernie Moreno was elected to chair the National Republican Senatorial Committee. Thune will lead Republicans in the minority when the new Congress begins.
candidates.title: Senate Republicans reelect John Thune as leader

candidates.summary: The Federal Trade Commission announced an amended complaint on November 10 adding Arizona, Florida, Nebraska, Ohio and Wisconsin to its pending lawsuit against Hims & Hers. The suit alleges improper sharing of sensitive health information with advertising platforms and deceptive billing and cancellation practices. California and Utah were already participating. The amended complaint adds allegations under the five additional states' consumer protection laws; the claims remain to be decided in federal court.
candidates.title: Five states join FTC privacy and billing lawsuit against Hims & Hers

candidates.summary: An eight-count superseding indictment unsealed on November 10 charged Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi, Mohsen Mohajeri and Mohammad Ali al-Hassani with terrorism-related offenses. US prosecutors alleged involvement in nearly 20 attacks and attempted attacks in Europe and the United States, including a September plot against RAF Fairford in Britain. Prosecutors alleged that al-Saadi attempted to coordinate the Fairford plot through coded communications while jailed in New York. Iran has denied involvement in the suspected plot; the charges are allegations, not findings of guilt.
candidates.title: US unseals charges against three men over alleged Iran-linked attacks
candidates.geography: United States; United Kingdom; Iran; Europe

sources.name: US Attorney's Office, Southern District of New York

candidates.summary: The Ninth US Circuit Court of Appeals on November 10 upheld a ruling allowing eight former SpaceX engineers to pursue their lawsuit in court rather than private arbitration. The engineers allege they were fired after raising concerns about sexual harassment and discrimination. The appeals court held that their claims fell within a federal law exempting sexual harassment disputes from mandatory arbitration. SpaceX has denied the underlying allegations; the decision did not resolve their merits.
candidates.title: Appeals court rejects SpaceX arbitration request in fired engineers' lawsuit

candidates.summary: Spain's government said on November 10 that TikTok should suspend operations in the country until it eliminates child sexual abuse material. Youth Minister Sira Rego appealed to prosecutors and the Data Protection Agency following an investigation by Maldita.es. The ministry cannot unilaterally ban the platform, and the announcement did not establish that a suspension had been ordered. TikTok did not immediately respond to Reuters' request for comment.
candidates.title: Spain demands TikTok suspension over child sexual abuse material

candidates.summary: Oura announced on November 10 that it had agreed to acquire Counsel Health for $625 million in cash, subject to purchase-price adjustments. Counsel combines medical AI with access to physicians, and the companies said they planned to expand their existing partnership integrating Oura data with care services. The acquisition had not closed and remained subject to customary closing conditions.
candidates.title: Oura agrees to acquire Counsel Health for $625 million
